title: Find the celebrity
label: multi
statement: At a party of `n` people, a **celebrity** is someone everyone knows and who knows nobody. You can only call `knows(a, b)`. Return the celebrity's number, or `-1` if there is none — using **as few calls as possible**.
provenance: Reported in LinkedIn coding rounds on LeetCode Discuss (a first coding round, with a Number of Islands variation, and in another loop with tree problems). LeetCode 277.

sources.name: LeetCode Discuss — LinkedIn interview experiences (search summaries; individual post not identified)

clarify: Is there at most one celebrity? (Yes, by definition.)
Is knows(a, a) meaningful? (Never call it.)
How expensive is knows? (Very — count your calls.)

stages.title: Find them
stages.say: Find the celebrity, or say there is none.
stages.require: Implement `Celebrity.Find(n, knows)`; −1 if there is none.
testNames: two people who know each other
one person is trivially the celebrity

listen: Restates the problem and asks the clarifying questions that change the code (Is there at most one celebrity? (Yes, by definition.); Is knows(a, a) meaningful? (Never call it.))

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe one pass eliminates a candidate per call — if the candidate knows i, the candidate cannot be the celebrity — then a second pass verifies the survivor, so at most 3(n−1) calls to knows. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Find concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: At a party of `n` people, a **celebrity** is someone everyone knows and who knows nobody. You can only call `knows(a, b)`. Return the celebrity's number, or `-1` if there is none — using **as few calls as possible**.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Is there at most one celebrity? (Yes, by definition.)
- Is knows(a, a) meaningful? (Never call it.)
- How expensive is knows? (Very — count your calls.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Every call rules someone out: if a knows b, a is not the celebrity; if not, b is not. So n−1 calls leave one candidate — who still has to be verified, because "not ruled out" is not the same as "celebrity".

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "O."ne pass eliminates a candidate per call — if the candidate knows i, the candidate cannot be the celebrity — then a second pass verifies the survivor, so at most 3(n−1) calls to knows."

- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- The O(n²) check of every pair.
- Skipping the verification pass.
- Calling knows(i, i).
- Repeating calls you already made in the first pass (fine to say, cheaper to cache).
